display.purpose: Page h1 titles and large stat numbers. Barlow Semi Condensed 700, tracking -0.02em.

headline.purpose: SectionHeading — the label above a card or region.

body.purpose: Paragraphs, form values, table cells. Barlow 400.

label.purpose: Uppercase badge text and filter headers. Barlow 600, tracking 0.08em.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modal-style floating panels — the command palette, dialogs.

shadows.name: menu
shadows.purpose: Smaller detached surfaces — dropdown action menus, popovers, toasts.

motion.name: ease-snappy
motion.purpose: The only easing. State-change feedback on controls and surfaces.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Default transition length — hover, active, color and border changes.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Slightly longer changes where 100ms feels abrupt.

motion.name: splash-fade
motion.purpose: AppSplash overlay opacity fade-out on first visit only.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one accent-colored action per screen — 'Check all sites', 'Add', submit.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: 'Barlow Semi Condensed', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; padding: 8px 18px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 2px solid var(--accent, #e4312b); background: var(--accent, #e4312b); color: var(--accent-text, #ffffff); cursor: pointer; transition: all 100ms cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-hover, #c92620); border-color: var(--accent-hover, #c92620); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring, #e4312b); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral action — inverts to solid ink on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: 'Barlow Semi Condensed', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; padding: 8px 18px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 2px solid var(--border-strong, #000000); background: transparent; color: var(--text-primary, #000000); cursor: pointer; transition: all 100ms cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--surface-inverse, #000000); color: var(--text-inverse, #ffffff); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring, #e4312b); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Tag filter / sort toggle. Pill; fills with accent when active.
components.css: .ds-chip { font-family: 'Barlow', -apple-system, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid var(--border-default, #dcdcdc); background: transparent; color: var(--text-primary, #000000); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1); } .ds-chip:hover { background: var(--surface-sunken, #f7f7f7); } .ds-chip--active { border-color: var(--accent, #e4312b); background: var(--accent, #e4312b); color: var(--accent-text, #ffffff); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring, #e4312b); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Signature state marker — a colored dot plus label, one per site/check state.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Barlow', -apple-system, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; color: var(--status-up, #2f8f4e); } .ds-status__dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: currentColor; } .ds-status--down { color: var(--status-down, #e4312b); } .ds-status--degraded { color: var(--status-degraded, #a86a0e); } .ds-status--maint { color: var(--status-maint, #4a70a8); } .ds-status--neutral { color: var(--text-tertiary, #8f8f8f); }

components.name: Pill Badge
components.description: Uppercase status/label pill — tint fill, solid-color text, no border.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font-family: 'Barlow', -apple-system, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid transparent; background: var(--surface-sunken, #f7f7f7); color: var(--text-primary, #000000); } .ds-badge--maint { background: var(--status-maint-tint, #e9eff7); color: var(--status-maint, #4a70a8); } .ds-badge--up { background: var(--status-up-tint, #eaf6ee); color: var(--status-up, #2f8f4e); } .ds-badge--down { background: var(--status-down-tint, #fdecea); color: var(--status-down, #e4312b); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Labeled field. Border shifts to strong on focus; error turns it red.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Barlow', -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-field__label { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--text-secondary, #5c5c5c); } .ds-field__input { border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border-default, #dcdcdc); background: var(--surface-raised, #ffffff); padding: 12px 16px; font-size: 16px; color: var(--text-primary, #000000); outline: none; transition: border-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1); } .ds-field__input::placeholder { color: var(--text-tertiary, #8f8f8f); } .ds-field__input:focus { border-color: var(--border-strong, #000000); }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: Pill track holding pills; active segment is a solid inverse pill.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; padding: 4px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid var(--border-default, #dcdcdc); } .ds-seg__opt { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; border: none; background: transparent; font-family: 'Barlow', -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--text-secondary, #5c5c5c); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1); } .ds-seg__opt:hover { background: var(--surface-sunken, #f7f7f7); color: var(--text-primary, #000000); } .ds-seg__opt--active { background: var(--surface-inverse, #000000); color: var(--text-inverse, #ffffff); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat content container — 20px radius, 1px hairline, no shadow. Border promotes to strong on hover when it is a link.
components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 20px; background: var(--surface-raised, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--border-default, #dcdcdc); padding: 24px; transition: border-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1); } .ds-card--link:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong, #000000); }

narrative.overview: This is a monitoring dashboard built like a motorsport timing screen: monochrome at rest, dense with numbers, and readable at a glance while something is going wrong. The surface is pure black-and-white with a graphite mid-scale; the only chromatic voice is a single warm Surface 51 Red (#e4312b), spent carefully on the one primary action, the active nav item, the focus ring, the S51 mark, and genuine down/error state. Everything else earns its place through typography, hairline rule, and tonal surface steps. The typographic pairing is industrial and sturdy: Barlow Semi Condensed for every heading and numeric readout over plain Barlow for body copy. Nothing is decorative. Corners are either a full pill (every interactive control) or a calm container radius (8/12/20px). Motion is 100ms feedback on ease-snappy, never an entrance. Depth is almost flat: cards sit on the page with a 1px hairline border and no shadow, signaling interactivity by promoting that border to solid black on hover. The exception is transient floating layers (command palette, menus, toasts), which carry a single soft shadow. The persistent chrome is pure #000 in both themes by deliberate design.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome base, one signal-red accent used sparingly (~one prominent moment per screen)
Barlow Semi Condensed for all headings + numbers; Barlow for body
Full-pill interactive controls; 8/12/20px radius for containers
Flat by default — hairline borders and tonal surfaces, shadow only on floating layers
Snappy 100ms ease-snappy transitions as feedback, not decoration
Always-black sidebar/top bar in both light and dark themes
Five semantic status families (up / degraded / down / maintenance / neutral), each with a -tint pair

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Surface 51 Red appears on ~10% of a screen at most — one primary action, the active nav item, a focus ring, and any true down state. It is never a background wash, a large fill, a decorative divider, or a brand skin. Its rarity is what makes it mean 'look here.'

rules.name: The Constant Hue Rule
rules.body: Dark mode overrides the semantic layer only. The red-* and gray-* primitive scales and the accent hue are identical in both themes; only surface, border, and text roles are remapped.

rules.name: The Black Chrome Rule
rules.body: The sidebar and mobile top bar are #000 in both themes and are styled with literal colors (bg-black, text-white, border-white/15), never the flipping surface tokens.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Anything numeric that a user scans under pressure — uptime %, response ms, counts, Lighthouse scores — is set in Barlow Semi Condensed, not the body face. Numbers are display type here.

rules.name: The Two Tracking Rule
rules.body: Headings and readouts use tight tracking (-0.02em); uppercase labels use wide tracking (0.08em). Body text stays at normal. There is no other letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Flat-Bed Rule
rules.body: If it is part of the page, it is flat with a border. If it floats above the page (overlay, menu, toast), it gets exactly one shadow from the vocabulary — never both a heavy border and a shadow.

rules.name: The Border Promotion Rule
rules.body: Hover and active states on surfaces are expressed by moving the border from hairline to border-strong, or by swapping fill to the inverse surface — not by shadow, translate, or scale. Buttons may active:scale-[0.97] as touch feedback only.

dos: Do build every interactive control as a full pill (9999px) — buttons, chips, badges, segmented controls, tab nav, nav items, count dots.
Do use the 8 / 12 / 20px container radius for anything that holds content, and nothing between pill and those steps.
Do convey depth with a 1px hairline border and tonal surface steps (page -> raised -> sunken); promote the border to border-strong on hover instead of adding a shadow.
Do reserve shadow for transient floating layers (command palette, menus, toasts) using the Overlay / Menu vocabulary — one shadow, no heavy border.
Do show every up / degraded / down / paused / maintenance state with the StatusBadge dot + label pattern and the five semantic status colors.
Do set headings and any scanned number in Barlow Semi Condensed with -0.02em tracking; set uppercase labels in Barlow with 0.08em tracking.
Do keep transitions at ~100ms on ease-snappy (cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1)) — motion is feedback, not an entrance.
Do keep the sidebar and top bar #000 in both themes, styled with literal colors, not the flipping surface tokens.
Do limit Surface 51 Red to ~one prominent moment per screen (primary action, active nav, focus ring, S51 mark) plus genuine down/error state.
donts: Don't use the red as a large fill, background wash, gradient, or decorative divider — it is a signal, not a brand skin.
Don't put a drop shadow on a resting surface (card, panel, summary bar, input).
Don't introduce a second display typeface, a serif, or any letter-spacing outside the tight/normal/wide trio.
Don't invent a status color outside the five families (up / degraded / down / maint / neutral) and their -tint pairs.
Don't let dark mode alter the raw red-* / gray-* scales or the accent hue — only the semantic surface/border/text roles remap.
Don't exceed the 1160px content column or drop the 236px rail at desktop.
Don't signal hover/active with translate, scale, or shadow on surfaces — use border promotion or an inverse-fill swap (buttons' active:scale-[0.97] touch feedback is the only exception).
